## Clinical Trials Now Enrolling

#### CALL FOR PATIENTS: Clinical Trial for Soft Tissue Sarcoma in Dogs

Study Title: Feasibility and dose-optimization clinical trial of local immunotherapy for solid tumors in canine cancer patients

Eligibility: Any dog weighing 5kg or above with at least one cutaneous soft tissue sarcoma lesion that is greater than 1.7cm in diameter is eligible to enroll. All dogs that meet the study criteria will receive the study drug (no placebo) followed by surgical removal of the tumor 1 week later.

Study Purpose: This clinical trial evaluates the safety, feasibility, and biological effects of a newly designed immunotherapy. Specifically, the study is evaluating the injection of investigational T-cell engagers (TCEs) directly into tumors (intratumorally) in canine patients with soft tissue sarcoma (STS). TCEs are engineered antibodies that physically connect T cells to cancer cells by targeting specific markers (CD3 or CD28 on T cells, and B7-H3 or PD-L1 on cancer cells), triggering the immune system to destroy tumor cells.
Dogs must not have any other serious concurrent illness.

  * Owners must be willing to commit to the study visit schedule over a 130-day duration.
  * Owners will be required to assess their dog for and record clinical signs of CIE and any unfavorable events their dog experiences during the study.
  * Dogs that are diagnosed with CIE after the screening workup will either get a novel medication for CIE or get a placebo. After the conclusion of the study (130 days) we can transition to standard therapy for CIE. This medication has been tested in healthy animals and found to be safe.
  * All Study related costs will be covered by the trial Sponsor.

#### FELINE CANCER STUDY:
Enrollment Now Closed

Veterinary Referral Center of Central Oregon concluded a clinical trial including cats with any solid tumor type that may be amenable to treatment with chemotherapy. Patients are candidates for screening even if they have received prior chemotherapy or other cancer treatments as long as they have not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy within 3 weeks of starting the study.

ImageTrial now recruiting · Australia

# Register your interest in our dog cancer trial

We are recruiting dogs with mast cell cancer in Australia for an investigational trial of personalised mRNA cancer vaccines. Register your interest and share a few details about your dog. Our team will contact you about further screening.

Why we are running this trial

## From Rosie’s story to a future for more dogs.

Image: Rosie

Rosie

The first dog treated with a personalised neoantigen vaccine.

It began with Rosie. Her experience with a personalised neoantigen vaccine encouraged Paul to explore how this approach could one day be made available to every dog with cancer.

Before an approach like this can become broadly available, we must study it carefully and support it by evidence for review by the relevant veterinary regulators. This clinical trial is an important step in that process, helping us learn from participating dogs and understand the vaccine more fully.

Read Rosie’s personalised mRNA cancer-vaccine story  →

Who can register

## If your dog has cancer and is currently in Australia, you’re welcome to register your interest. Our team will check whether your dog may be eligible for this trial.

Register your interest  →

About the trial

## What this trial is looking at

The trial will investigate a personalised mRNA vaccine approach for dogs with mast cell cancer. Tell us about your dog and our team will help determine whether they may be eligible for screening.

Image

### Who can register

Dogs diagnosed with mast cell cancer who are based in, or able to travel within, Australia.

Every case is reviewed individually

Image

### The trial approach

A therapeutic mRNA vaccine designed from each dog’s own tumour and blood samples, intended to work alongside—not replace—existing care.

Personalised to each dog

Image

### What screening involves

We help coordinate records, screening, sample logistics and updates, working with the trial team and your treating veterinarian.

A named team stays in touch

Trial registration and screening

## How to register your interest.

You don’t need to have every record ready before registering your interest. Start with what you know and we’ll help with the rest.

01

### Register your interest

Complete a short form with basic details about your dog, their mast cell cancer diagnosis and where you live.

02

### We get in touch

A Gamgee coordinator will contact you, answer practical questions and—with your permission—help gather relevant records from your vet.

03

### The trial team confirms eligibility

The authorised study team and treating veterinarian assess potential eligibility. If your dog may proceed, you’ll receive the approved trial information and consent discussion before deciding.

These are indicative timings from a single case. Sequencing turnaround and manufacturing schedules may vary. We will give you a case-specific estimate before proceeding.

## Ready to tell us about your dog?

Registering your interest does not guarantee eligibility or enrolment. Please continue your dog's existing veterinary care while your information is reviewed.

Register your interest  →

# Current clinical trials

We have many opportunities for pet animals to participate in clinical trials. Each listing below has a quick summary plus a link to more information for each study.

## AMPs: canine pyoderma topical treatment study

A canine clinical trial to test the efficacy and safety of superficial pyoderma using a ceragnin-based hydrogel.

Species

Dog

Category

Dermatology

Current Status

Open and enrolling

## Canine Brain Tumor Program

Leading edge research combined with compassionate care

Species

Dog

Category

Neurology

Current Status

Open and enrolling

## CAR-T cell therapy for canines with B-cell lymphoma

A canine clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a CAR-T cell therapy product for the treatment B-cell lymphoma

Species

Dog

Category

Cancer/Oncology

Current Status

Open and enrolling

## Lyra 1 - blood collection study for lymphoma

A minimally invasive blood sampling study to identify dogs at high risk of developing Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). Samples must be collected at the University of Minnesota, Small Animal Hospital.

Species

Dog

Category

Cancer/Oncology

Current Status

Ongoing but enrollment closed

## LYRA 3 - blood collection study for lymphoma in healthy dogs at least 5 years old

This project aims to create a simple blood test that can accurately check if a healthy dog has undetected diffuse large b-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or is at high risk of developing it. In the future, this test could be paired with targeted treatments to prevent tumors from developing. 

Species

Dog

Category

Cancer/Oncology

Current Status

Open and enrolling

## New vaccine for dogs with oral melanoma

Novel adeno-associated virus (AAV) vaccine for dogs with malignant oral melanoma

Species

Dog

Category

Cancer/Oncology

Current Status

Open and enrolling

## Olaparib + Meloxicam for Feline Mammary Carcinoma

A pilot clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of combination olaparib and meloxicam therapy for treatment of feline mammary carcinoma

Species

Cat

Category

Cancer/Oncology

Current Status

Open and enrolling

## ORBIT - VSV and an anti-PD-1 inhibitor for Canine Lymphoma

This study hopes to understand how a new combination immunotherapy works and to determine if it is effective in the treatment for dogs with relapsed and refractory aggressive lymphoma. 

Species

Dog

Category

Cancer/Oncology

Current Status

Open and enrolling

## Puppy Gait Analysis Study

A canine clinical trial to evaluate gait development and coordination in puppies into adulthood.

Species

Dog

Category

Orthopedics/Surgery

Current Status

Open and enrolling

## Shine On Continuation

Study for dogs to test eBAT prevention of cancer

Species

Dog

Category

Cancer/Oncology

Current Status

Completed

ESVONC attaches great importance to innovation and evidence-based medicine in the field of veterinary oncology. Therefore, we are happy to share with you with a monthly overview of ongoing canine and feline oncology trials in Europe. We are convinced that knowledge of these trials will enhance collaboration between researchers and clinicians, thus increasing recruitment for clinical trials and treatment options for dogs and cats.
Please find below a non-exhaustive listing of ongoing trials as gathered in the Oncowaf database. For more details about these trials, please visit https://oncowaf.be/en/ClinicalTrials.

If you have an ongoing clinical trial and would like to add it to the Oncowaf clinical trial database and this mailing, please contact contact@oncowaf.com. This list is an intiative of dr. Laetitia Cicchelero (DVM, PhD, Cross-health coordinator @ Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Ghent University). Laetitia is initiator and inspirer of ONCOWAF. ESVONC wishes to thank Laetitia for her efforts to create this useful overview.
